The Past Continuous Tense
You use the Past Continuous tense to talk about an action that was happening (in progress) at a time before now.
You can use the Past Continuous to:
• to describe the background in a story written in the past tense

For example:
“The children were laughing and the birds were singing in the park. A woman was looking for her phone, which she dropped somewhere ... ”
• to describe an action that was interrupted by another event or action

For example:
One day a traveler was passing by the tailor's shop and heard him singing.
• to describe two actions in progress in the past

For example:
While I was looking at the fabric, I was thinking about how I could make myself a warm coat!
The form of the Past Continuous is:
Subject + was/were + verb-ing
While I was looking at the fabric, I was thinking about how I could make myself a warm coat!
Unfortunately, while I was working,the scissors slipped, cut, and ruined it.
The traveler peeked into the shop to see what was going on.
One day a traveler was passing by the tailor's shop and heard him singing.
While I was cutting the cloth, I realized that I'd cut away too much.
The Simple Past Tense
You use the Simple Past tense to talk about many kinds of past events: short, quickly finished actions, longer situations and repeated events.
Usually, when you use the Simple Past tense, the time of the finished action is clear from the context or explicitly mentioned in the sentence.
For example:
Once there was a tailor, who was poor, but always happy and positive about life.
You can use the Simple Past with the Past Continuous to talk about an action that interrupted another action in progress in the past.
For example:
While I was cutting the cloth, I realized that I'd cut away too much.
The event of “realizing” interrupts the action of “cutting”.
Remember that there are both regular and irregular verbs. Look at the chart for examples of the Simple Past tense verbs.

Once there was a tailor, who was poor, but always happy and positive about life. He wasn't getting much business, because he didn't have money to buy cloth.
One day a traveler was passing by the tailor's shop and heard him singing. The traveler peeked into the shop to see what was going on. The tailor was sitting next to a pile of scrap material, singing a song about a jacket.

"What are you singing about?" the traveler asked.
The tailor looked up in surprise. "Have a seat," he said. "I'll tell you how it came about!"

So it was that the tailor began his tale.
"Some time ago, a man came to me. He asked me to make him a suit. He disappeared before I could take his measurements, but he left the material behind.

While I was looking at the fabric, I was thinking about how I could make myself a warm coat! Now that I had the material to do it!

“While I was cutting the cloth, I realized that I'd cut away too much. So, I decided to make a jacket instead. I began to fashion the jacket, but soon found that I'd cut away too much again. Hence, I decided to make a vest.

I designed, cut, and began to sew.Unfortunately, while I was working,the scissors slipped, cut, and ruined it. Here lie the pieces. There's not enough material for a garment, but there is enough material for a song! La di la di, la la."
